_readme: GAME CONTENT: how PvE encounters are put together from enemy-library.json. Shapes are generated encounters: the runtime EncounterGenerator picks a variant (by Weight), draws each slot's count in [Min, Max] and each unit's type uniformly from Types, and keeps the draw only if its summed enemy Threat is inside [ThreatMin, ThreatMax], it has at least MinDistinctTypes types and it seats on the arena; units are placed front to back (Vanguard, Skirmisher, Ranged; library order within a stance). Each lineup then draws an element scheme by SchemeWeights (Uniform: one element for the whole team; PerType: one per type; PerUnit: one per unit; None), with elements dealt from a shuffled deck of the ten so every element is dealt before any repeats. Shape ids are drop-tables.json's shape ids (the validator requires the two sets to match): a cleared encounter pays out from its shape's drop cell. Templates are authored fixed encounters ({ EncounterId, DisplayName, Description, ShapeId, Arena, Groups: [{ EnemyId, Count, Elements }], DifficultyOverride, Draft }; Elements are cycled over the group, empty = no element; DifficultyOverride 0 = use the shape's calibrated difficulty; Draft true = placeholder text/design pending producer review, never shown to the player). The ten region bosses (regions.json's BossTemplateId) are the only templates, DRAFT placeholders pending producer review; each DifficultyOverride is calibrated so a scouting team at the boss's level wearing typical gear clears about 50% (docs/balance/tuning-log.md). Difficulty: every enemy's HP, Attack, Defense, SpecialAttack and SpecialDefense are multiplied by the shape's calibrated multiplier at the encounter's level (encounter-difficulty.json, written by the balance simulator's --write-difficulty, interpolated between the calibrated levels) times DifficultyScale. PENDING PRODUCER REVIEW: DifficultyScale is 1.0 and the table is calibrated so a player who scouts and counter-picks (the simulator's bond-aware heuristic pick) wearing typical gear (the balance simulator's --gear typical, a user decision) clears each shape's TargetClear (the tiered targets, a user decision: squad and horde 80%, elite 60%, solo 50%; encounter-difficulty.json records the target of every cell); whether the campaign should be that hard, and how a map node picks a shape and a level, are producer decisions not made here. Validated by EncounterLibraryValidator (the Editor importer Beast Craft/Data/Import Encounters, the EditMode tests, Tooling/BalanceSim): every shape's worst case (each slot at Max, each unit its slot's largest type) and every template must fit its arena's enemy deployment zone. The shapes and weights came over unchanged from the balance simulator's former fixtures; see docs/design/battle-system.md, 'Encounter direction'. Boss names and descriptions follow docs/design/content-bible.md; each boss carries Draft: true until the producer signs it off (the validator rejects a [DRAFT] marker in DisplayName/Description, which are player-facing); the calibration note that used to sit in each Description is this readme's (each DifficultyOverride clears about 50% for a scouting team at the boss's level in typical gear).

Shapes.Description: One giant: huge HP, heavy single-target hits in both categories every turn and a periodic area slam in both. Compositions differ only in the giant's element.
A boss with an escort: one giant and two standard enemies, or two champions (mini-bosses) and one or two standard enemies.
Four to six standard enemies of at least three types: melee tanks, hunters, archers, casters and shamans.

Sixteen to twenty-four enemies: mostly swarm (tiny melee: swarmlings bite, physical; stinglings sting, special; one skill each, since every hit deals at least the damage floor), with a few archers and casters behind them.

Templates.Description: A moss-backed champion that once guarded the Hollow's Seal for the first Beastbinders and now guards it from everyone. Two horned brutes stamp at its side.
Twin fire champions who fight back to back on the ridge, trading sparks and grudges, while two archers pepper the field from the rocks above.
A barnacled water giant risen from the drowned ruins, with two casters chanting tide and frost from the shallows at its feet.
An air giant who walks the cloud line wrapped in its own gale, while three stalkers slip through the wind to pounce on stragglers.
Two great antlered champions, one of iron and one of stone, lock horns with anyone who nears the Seal. A shaman and two brutes keep the herd.
A towering ice giant who shelters a skittering brood of ten swarmlings under her skirts of snow, while two archers watch from the drifts.
The lightning giant holds court on the highest spire, a gale champion at its right hand and two casters crackling at its back.
The oldest living thing in the Deepwild: a nature giant grown half into the forest, wrapped in a humming cloud of twelve stinglings and tended by two shamans.
A fire giant crowned in cooling lava who sits the volcano's throne, flanked by two champions of stone and iron.
Two ancient giants, one of fire and one of water, who have guarded the Worldcrown's summit together since the first Seal was set. Where they meet, the Gloam rises.
